The Cottages at Bridal Falls / Bridal Falls RV Resort — 53480 Bridal Falls Road

A gated bare-land strata resort community. MLS listing records for lots and cottages at this address state the tenure directly: "Title to Land: Freehold Strata," subdivision name "The Cottages At Bridal Falls," zoning CD1, with serviced lots (gas, hydro, water, sewer), concrete pads, and full-time or lock-and-go use; listing text describes it as an "exclusive, gated, bareland strata community" with clubhouse, outdoor pool, hot tub, fitness centre and tennis courts among the amenities, and cottage units on the lots are recorded as single-family / rancher form on freehold strata lots — land and cottage product, not apartment condos, and not counted above. A 2020 developer-era advertisement described the resort as 100 lots on almost 8 acres — advertising copy, carried as such.

items.t: Bridal Falls is a small unincorporated community in the Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area D (Popkum–Bridal Falls), east of the City of Chilliwack, near Rosedale and Popkum, at the Highway 1 / Highway 9 interchange area; the FVRD, not the City of Chilliwack, is its local government for planning, zoning, building inspection and bylaw enforcement.
Market statistics: none are quoted for this area.
Where the strata stock concentrates: at one address — 53480 Bridal Falls Road, the gated bare-land strata resort community the listings call Bridal Falls RV Resort / The Cottages at Bridal Falls.

Transit: BC Transit route 71 (Agassiz–Harrison) runs between Downtown Chilliwack and Harrison Hot Springs through Rosedale, and its on-request trips can route to Bridal Falls — Trip Note B on BC Transit's own Route 71 route-overview page states: "On-Request trips can route to Bridal Falls and/or the Community and Cultural Recreation Centre in Agassiz" — so Bridal Falls is served on request rather than by a fixed stop on every trip; no other BC Transit route serving it was confirmed.

Parks and services: Bridal Veil Falls Provincial Park, a day-use park on the south side of the Fraser River, 16 km east of Chilliwack, reached by Exit 135 off Highway 1 — the falls tumble 60 metres over a smooth rock face and BC Parks warns the base is extremely hazardous. Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park (FVRD), 53480 Elgey Road, Rosedale, is a 107-hectare park of lake, marsh and forest in Electoral Area D where 184 bird species have been recorded and pets are not permitted under FVRD Bylaw No. 1500, 2018.

items.t: RURAL property taxes govern here — the staged provincial regime, not a city regime: Bridal Falls is unincorporated, so property taxes are levied under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act: taxes in a notice mailed on or before May 31 are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to taxes unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% to taxes still unpaid on October 31 (s. 11). For contrast only — explicitly NON-governing — the City of Chilliwack's second penalty stage falls after August 4, 2026, and the City of Mission's regime is a flat 10% after July 2; neither applies in Electoral Area D.

ALR frame: on ALR land the principal residence maximum is a total floor area of 500 m²; a secondary suite is permitted only when entirely contained within the principal residence and local bylaws permit it; and one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, subject to local bylaws. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). Parcel-level ALR status for any specific Bridal Falls property: confirm on the ALC's ALR maps.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), for the park product nearby: pad-rent increases in a manufactured home park are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027. That regime applies to pad tenancies like Mt Cheam's — it does not apply to the freehold strata lots at 53480 Bridal Falls Road, which have strata fees instead of pad rent.

blocks.text: How Bridal Falls got its name, and what is here today

Bridal Falls takes its name from Bridal Veil Falls, but the post office could not. When the community asked for a "Bridal Veil Falls" post office, the name was already taken elsewhere in Canada, so the office that opened on November 1, 1937 was called Bridal Falls instead. The Province adopted the name for the post office in 1950 and has recognised Bridal Falls as an official community since July 15, 1983.

The falls themselves sit in Bridal Veil Falls Park, a day-use provincial park on the south side of the Fraser River, 16 km east of Chilliwack, reached from exit 135 on Highway 1. The water drops 60 metres over a smooth rock face. In cold winters the falls can freeze into an unstable wall of ice, and BC Parks warns that the base becomes hazardous, with falling ice and rock, so a winter visit is a look from the viewing area rather than a walk to the bottom.

The park is a day-use area with picnic tables, drinking water and toilets, and dogs are welcome on a leash. It is run for BC Parks by a private operator, Sea to Sky Park Services, which is who to call about closures or conditions.

For a buyer, Bridal Falls is the highway-service end of Electoral Area D: the exit, the park, fuel, restaurants and tourist stops sit close to the homes. Owners get the scenery and quick access to Highway 1 and to the bridge north to Agassiz and Highway 9. Area D as a whole had 2,299 residents in the 2021 Census across 223 square kilometres, so homes here come up for sale only a few times a year.

items.t: Local government / plan — FVRD: Bridal Falls is in FVRD Electoral Area D (Popkum–Bridal Falls); the FVRD provides planning and development approvals, building inspection and bylaw enforcement for its electoral areas — City of Chilliwack zoning does not apply here.
Zoning — FVRD: the FVRD sets zoning for Electoral Area D.
The process is documented instead: subdivision and servicing questions go to the FVRD as the electoral-area authority; no bylaw number is asserted.

ALR block: subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha), subject to local bylaws.

Strata block (the bare-land strata at 53480 Bridal Falls Road): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page — for a bare-land strata lot the Form B package (fees, amounts owing, special levies, CRF balance, insurance, rules, budget, Rental Disclosure Statement, depreciation report) is what establishes the fees and registered rules; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024 (a resort with clubhouse, pool and serviced lots carries exactly the common-property assets a depreciation report prices); minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023; rental bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

Taxes — RURAL regime applies (FVRD electoral area, not a municipality): under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11, a 5% penalty applies after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31. Chilliwack's municipal penalty dates and Mission's flat 10% do not apply to this area.
